gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: Buggies are allowed right across the site, but there’s no buggy park, so I would bring one you’re happy to keep with you all day. The shuttle buses at the big Air Shows take a limited number of unfolded buggies.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Only guide dogs and assistance dogs are allowed, and that includes the car parks. Please leave pet dogs at home, as a car gets far too hot on a show day.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: Packed lunches and picnics are fine, but barbecues aren’t. When I last checked, the rules didn’t say whether you can bring your own alcohol, so I would ask IWM before you pack any, as there are licensed bars on site.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Folding chairs, picnic blankets and a properly secured windbreak are fine, and small tents are allowed if they don’t block anyone’s view. Large tents, gazebos, stools and step ladders aren’t.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: There are free water points across the site. I would bring a refillable bottle and top it up through the day, especially on the crowd line.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There’s a registered Changing Places toilet in Hangar 1, next to the Visitor Centre. It opens with a Radar key, and staff or volunteers can lend you one.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: Disabled visitors can bring a carer free of charge. You book the free carer ticket at the same time as your own, and I would bring your documentation on the day, dated within the last two years.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: Hearing loops are fitted at the Visitor Centre admissions desk and shop, Hangar 1, the American Air Museum and Historic Duxford, and the films in Hangar 1 and Historic Duxford have BSL. I couldn’t see anything about BSL for the show commentary, so I would ask IWM before you go.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: There’s a Quiet Room behind the 19 Squadron Restaurant, and sensory backpacks with ear defenders can be borrowed free from the Visitor Centre and the Visit Planning Point in Hangar 1. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: The ticket rules say a ticket that has already been used will be refused at the gate. So I would plan on staying in once you’re through, and if you really need to pop back to the car, ask a steward at the gate first.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: First aid is in the Green Zone, and children must be with an adult at all times. I would agree a meeting point as soon as you arrive and tell the nearest steward straight away if you get separated.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. The hangars are the best shelter on site, and there are no refunds if a show is called off because of the weather.

days.html:
Pick Your Show

Duxford has seven flying events in 2027, and they feel quite different from each other. The two big Air Shows are the full day out, with the biggest line-ups, the flightline walk and the crowds to match. The Flying Days, the Flying Evening and the Flying Finale are smaller and calmer. Answer a few quick questions and I’ll tell you which one I would pick for you.

Events in 2027Seven
Season8 May to 2 October
Big Air ShowsJune and September
TicketsAdvance only

The Bigger Shows

Summer Air ShowSaturday 19 and Sunday 20 June. Site open 08:00 to 19:00, with the broadest mix of the season. You’ll need a parking permit, and there’s a free shuttle from Cambridge.
Battle Of Britain Air ShowSaturday 11 and Sunday 12 September. The summer of 1940 on the airfield where it happened, with Spitfires, Hurricanes and the Big Wing. The same permit and shuttle set up as June.
Flying EveningSaturday 14 August. In 2026 it ran 17:00 to 21:30, with formation aerobatics and airborne pyrotechnics as the light goes. Parking on site, no booking.
Flying FinaleSaturday 2 October. The last show of the year, looking back at the best of the season. In 2026 it ran 10:00 to 18:00. Parking on site, no booking.

The Flying Days

VE DaySaturday 8 May, 10:00 to 18:00. Up to two hours of flying marking the road to victory in 1945.
D-DaySaturday 5 June, 10:00 to 18:00. Up to two hours of flying telling the D-Day story.
The AmericansLater in the summer, built around the wartime link between the US and Britain. It sits nicely with a wander round the American Air Museum. I would check the date on the IWM calendar.
Good To KnowFree for IWM members, and booked in advance like every Duxford event. There’s no shuttle bus, but parking is on site with no booking.

Who’s coming?

What are you after?

Are you an IWM member?

How are you getting there?

I Would Pick The Summer Air Show

  1. WhyIt’s the broadest mix of the year, with the full big show set up: traders, living history, the hangars and the flightline walk in the morning. Children love to see the aircraft up close on the flightline before a single engine starts.
  2. Good to knowWhen I last checked, children 15 and under went free with a Standard Adult ticket, and every ticket covers the museum hangars. Your child’s ears are delicate, so try to protect them as much as possible.
  3. Getting thereBook your parking permit with your ticket, because you can’t turn up and park without one. By train, the free shuttle runs from Cambridge station and Trumpington Park and Ride. More in .

I Would Pick The Battle Of Britain Air Show

  1. WhyIf 1940 is what gets you, this is the one. Watching Spitfires and Hurricanes fly from the same grass as 19 Squadron is hard to beat, and the Big Wing is the moment I would wait for.
  2. Good to knowIt gets busy. If you want a front row seat, head to the crowd line first and save your pitch, then do the flightline walk before it closes at about 12 noon. Visit the toilet before the flying starts.
  3. Getting thereSame as June. A parking permit booked with your ticket, or the free shuttle from Cambridge station and Trumpington Park and Ride. More in .

I Would Pick A Flying Day

  1. WhyYou get a taster of the big shows, with up to two hours of flying and far fewer people. This may work for you if you aren’t sure how a full Air Show day would go with little ones.
  2. Good to knowFlying Days run 10:00 to 18:00 and they’re free for IWM members, though you still book in advance. I would choose by theme: VE Day in May, D-Day in June or The Americans later in the summer.
  3. Getting thereParking is on site with no booking. There’s no free shuttle on these days, so if you’re coming by train, take a look at the bus and taxi options in .

I Would Pick The Flying Evening

  1. WhyIt’s shorter and more relaxed, and the light as the sun drops is lovely. In 2026 it ran 17:00 to 21:30, with formation aerobatics and airborne pyrotechnics. A great one for photographers.
  2. Good to knowWhen I last checked, you needed a normal entrance ticket to look round before 17:00, so think about whether you want the hangars too. It gets chilly as the light goes, so I would pack a jumper.
  3. Getting thereParking is on site with no booking, and there’s no shuttle bus. More in .

I Would Pick The Flying Finale

  1. WhyIt wraps up the season with a look back at its highlights, and the crowds are smaller than the big shows. If you’ve followed Duxford all year, this is a nice way to finish.
  2. Good to knowIn 2026 it ran 10:00 to 18:00, and IWM members got 10% off. October can be fresh on an open airfield, so think about layers and a flask.
  3. Getting thereParking is on site with no booking, and there’s no shuttle bus. More in .
Jack’s tipI would book the two big Air Shows as early as you can. Parking permits are limited and there are no tickets on the gate, so leaving it late can catch you out. For the smaller events, you can be a bit more relaxed, but you still have to book.

Times and prices may change for 2027. Where I’ve given 2026 times, the 2027 ones are still to be published.
